rules.name: Next-candle bias starts from how price closes relative to the previous candle range
rules.setupAnchor: Previous candle high and low define the reference range
rules.confirmationTrigger: A close outside the previous candle range implies continuation bias, while a sweep and close back inside implies reversal bias
rules.protectedSwingDefinition: Lower-timeframe protected swing logic should be interpreted inside the active higher-timeframe bias rather than replacing it
rules.invalidationCondition: A new candle closes in the opposite structural mode or a lower-timeframe execution setup directly contradicts the higher-timeframe bias
rules.targetLogic: Continuation bias seeks expansion beyond the swept side; reversal bias seeks movement back into or across the prior range
exceptions: After several same-direction continuation candles, expect a new phase instead of forcing another continuation
pineInputsNeeded: sweep state relative to previous candle range
machineChecks: Detect close above previous high or below previous low
Detect sweep beyond previous high or low followed by close back inside the prior range
Store current bias mode as continuation or reversal
ambiguityNotes: Bias is cleaner on daily and four-hour charts than on lower noisy timeframes

rules.name: Reversal-day bias is framed from previous day highs or lows plus lower-timeframe confirmation
rules.setupAnchor: Price trades into the previous day high or low after a directional prior-day close
rules.confirmationTrigger: A wick forms at the prior-day extreme and the lower timeframe confirms a change in the state of delivery
rules.protectedSwingDefinition: The lower-timeframe shift that confirms the wick becomes the structural reference for executing the reversal thesis
rules.invalidationCondition: The wick fails to hold or lower-timeframe structure continues through the prior-day level without the confirming shift
rules.targetLogic: First target is equilibrium of the previous day range; extended target is the opposite side of the prior range
exceptions: A large wick does not support immediate opposite expansion and often requires waiting for candle three or the next candle
If higher-timeframe bias points the other way, the move may only be a retracement instead of a full reversal
machineChecks: Mark prior-day high and low as reversal anchors
Measure whether the higher-timeframe candle sweeps a prior-day extreme and closes back inside or rejects from it
Require lower-timeframe confirmation before execution mode is active
ambiguityNotes: CISD still needs a stricter algorithmic definition
Wick-size threshold for immediate reversal versus delayed confirmation is not yet numeric

rules.name: Continuation-day bias uses prior candle closure plus equilibrium respect
rules.setupAnchor: Previous day directional close establishes continuation intent and equilibrium defines the area of interest
rules.confirmationTrigger: Price opens, retraces toward equilibrium or a point of interest, respects it without lower-timeframe closes beyond, then continues through the previous day high or low
rules.protectedSwingDefinition: Continuation structure becomes stronger once lower-timeframe continuation logic prints a protected swing in the direction of the higher-timeframe bias
rules.invalidationCondition: Price closes through equilibrium in the wrong direction or fails to continue through the previous day range objective
rules.targetLogic: Primary objective is continuation through the previous day high or low and then external liquidity in the same direction
exceptions: Respecting equilibrium does not require an exact touch
Rather than guessing which point of interest reacts, allow structure to confirm naturally
machineChecks: Compute equilibrium as midpoint of previous day range
Detect whether lower-timeframe closes remain on the correct side of equilibrium
Require continuation through the previous day directional objective
ambiguityNotes: The exact tolerance around equilibrium is not yet numeric

rules.name: Wick size filters whether the current candle supports expansion or reversion
rules.setupAnchor: Current candle open, high, low, and close define body and opposing wick
rules.confirmationTrigger: A small opposing run or wick supports expansion; a large opposing run suggests reversal, return to open, or limited range
rules.protectedSwingDefinition: Protected-swing confirmation has more value when the higher-timeframe candle also supports expansion through a small opposing run
rules.invalidationCondition: A candle that spends most of its time creating a large opposing wick should not be treated as a clean expansion candle
rules.targetLogic: Expansion-supporting candles justify continuation and farther targets; large-wick candles justify reduced targets such as the open or nearby liquidity
exceptions: The most reliable setup is often the next candle after the reversal candle, once a new small-wick expansion candle appears
machineChecks: Compute body size and opposing wick ratio
Classify whether the candle closes near its directional extreme or near its open
Switch expected target model based on small-wick versus large-wick classification
ambiguityNotes: The boundary between small and large opposing runs is not yet numeric
Time usage within the candle is conceptually important but not yet codified from OHLC alone

rules.name: Higher-timeframe bias filters all lower-timeframe entries
rules.setupAnchor: Higher timeframe establishes continuation or reversal expectation
rules.confirmationTrigger: Intermediate or lower timeframe confirms structure in the same direction as the higher timeframe thesis
rules.protectedSwingDefinition: Lower-timeframe protected swings are only execution tools unless they align with the higher-timeframe bias
rules.invalidationCondition: Lower-timeframe entry logic conflicts with the higher-timeframe candle behavior and bias framework
rules.targetLogic: Use the higher timeframe for direction and the lower timeframe for precision, not independent trade direction
exceptions: Below the four-hour chart, reversals become noisier and less reliable
Session choice changes the preferred lower timeframe for confirmation
pineInputsNeeded: session bucket or preferred execution window
machineChecks: Store higher-timeframe bias as a state variable
Reject lower-timeframe execution signals that oppose the active bias
Allow configurable execution timeframe mapping by session or user selection
ambiguityNotes: Session-to-timeframe mapping should be configurable rather than hard-coded
The project still needs a strict lower-timeframe CISD implementation

openQuestions: What numeric threshold best separates small and large opposing wicks for the bias framework?
How much tolerance around equilibrium should count as respect versus violation?
What is the strictest first-pass CISD implementation that remains useful across timeframes?
